text: In this activity, we are going to create our first graph network using Neo4j.
Before going into Neo4j, let's take a look at the following graph.
In this graph, we have nodes which represent people, and we have the edges between those nodes that represent the relationships between these people.
For example, we have a node N1 that represents Tom, we have another node N2 that represents
Harry, and the relationship between them is connected by the HE1, which says that the
relationship is that they know each other.
Our goal with this graph is to be able to build a script that we can process in Neo4j
and create an actual graph network.
In order to build our script, we are going to start by doing a simple text representation
like the one that we have right here with the five nodes and edges.
After a simple representation in which we only listed the nodes on one side and the
edges on the other, we can proceed with a more structured representation connecting
the nodes through the edges that represent these relationships.
Then we can proceed to make a more technical representation of our network in the form
of technical pseudocode.
In this case, we are introducing one class called ToyNode that is going to be the main
class for our nodes.
Therefore, as we introduce nodes to the network, we also define them to be part of this class.
For example, in the first line, we are introducing two new nodes, n1 and n2, so we also specify
them to be part of this class.
But in the next line, since we already introduced n2, we don't need to repeat that statement,
and so on with the rest of the network.
We can take a step further and define our edges to be part of a class that we are calling
toy relation.
With our classes defined, we can proceed to add properties to these classes in the form
of key value pairs.
For example, let's look at the first line.
In the first line we are introducing the node n1 to be part of the class toy node and it
has one property.
This property has a key of name and the value of this key is Tom.
Then it is connected through a toy relation in which the key is relationship and the value
is nose with another node n2 which is also part of the class toy node and has one property
the name Harry, and so on with the rest of the network.
After making a few adjustments to the previous pseudocode,
this is the actual Cypher script that we're going to use to build our network in Neo4j.
With our code ready, we're going to open Neo4j,
running the Docker container as we did in a previous activity,
and we're going to take our Cypher code and paste it in this cell so we can define our network.
So we run it and we're going to see this message which indicate that we have added five labels,
we have created five new nodes, we have set 13 properties, and we have created
five relationships, all of these in 86 milliseconds.
Now that we have loaded our first graph into Neo4j, the first thing that we want to do
with it is to visualize it.
To do this, we are going to run the following command in which we are going to match all
of the nodes of the type toy node and we are going to return them along with their respective
edges.
We run this, and this is the graph which is identical to the graph that we took as an
inspiration for this activity.
If we hover over each particular node, we can see the properties of those nodes.
For example, in this node, we have the property Job, which is Plumber, and the name, which
is Julian, and the same with the relationships, indicating what is the nature of the relationship
between the nodes.
We can take a different look of this graph if we go to our left menu and we click on
text, this is going to display this table which is going to give us a similar view to the one that
we built when we did the text representation. We have notes on the left side, the relationship in
